reading.body:
Ten distinct insurance and liability categories now map AI governance failure to named individuals, from EU conformity penalties to D&O claims over AI risk oversight.

The pattern is a shift from corporate compliance to personal accountability. Directors and officers face claims for failing to oversee AI risk, while vendors face fines for export violations and medical software non-compliance. Each category converts a regulatory or operational failure into a defined insurable event.

Three of the ten categories tie directly to compute and power. Antitrust defence over accelerator supply allocation, export control penalties for hardware, and greenwashing claims over data centre carbon and power usage effectiveness disclosures all make physical infrastructure a liability surface. This matters for AI because compute and power infrastructure are now sources of legal exposure, not just operational cost.

The data does not show premiums, claim frequency, or whether these covers are actually purchased. It lists categories of exposure, not outcomes. It also does not indicate which jurisdictions beyond the EU, US states, and FDA are covered, so the geographic scope of this liability map remains incomplete.
